---
title: SDC Tools
---

`sdc-tools` returns the clocks an SDC creates. SDC is freeform Tcl, so the file
is evaluated in a real Tcl interpreter whose SDC commands are stubs: variables,
`[command]` substitution, `foreach`, `if`, and flow-generated scripts work as
authored, and unsupported constraints are recorded instead of failing the run.

## Requirement

Tcl **>= 8.6** (`tclsh8.6` or `tclsh` on `PATH`; `TCLSH=/path/to/tclsh`
overrides). Tcl is an environment prerequisite, like a C compiler — not a
Python package.

## Install

```bash
uv sync --dev
uv run sdc-tools --help
```

Or install the project from the repository:

```bash
uv tool install "open-eda-file-tools @ git+https://github.com/smprather/open-eda-file-tools.git"
```

## Command line

```bash
uv run sdc-tools clocks --sdc design.sdc
```

```text
clock	period	waveform	sources	generated_from	divide_by	multiply_by
clk	10	0 5	port:clk
```

`--format json` emits the same data as JSON; `--output PATH` writes it to a
file. Periods and waveforms are in the SDC's time unit (ns by convention).

## Python API

```python
from sdc_tools import clocks

for clock in clocks("design.sdc"):
    print(clock.name, clock.period, clock.sources)
```

A `Clock` carries `name`, `period`, `waveform`, `sources`, `generated_from`,
`divide_by`, `multiply_by`, `edges`, and `invert`.

## Clock-tree cells

`sdc-tools clock-cells` traces forward from each clock's source object through
DEF connectivity. A combinational cell whose input pin sits on a clock net is a
tree cell; its output nets are followed. Sequential cells end the trace and are
not listed. Liberty supplies pin directions and the `ff`/`latch` classification,
so a clock buffer is found by connectivity even when its name says nothing about
clocks.

```bash
uv run sdc-tools clock-cells \
  --sdc design.sdc --def design.def.gz --lib sg13g2_stdcell_typ_1p20V_25C.lib \
  --output clock_cells.txt
```

`--format json` writes a JSON list instead of one instance per line. The output
is exactly what `def-tools instances --clock-cells` consumes:

```bash
uv run def-tools instances \
  --lef design.lef --def design.def.gz \
  --lib sg13g2_stdcell_typ_1p20V_25C.lib \
  --clock-cells clock_cells.txt \
  --format parquet --output instances.parquet
```

The trace needs DEF + Liberty + SDC. LEF is not required: bounding boxes are the
instance writer's concern.

## Semantics

- Collections stay symbolic: `port:clk`, `pin:div/Q`, `net:clk`, `cell:u1`.
  Resolving them against a design is a separate step.
- `create_clock`: `-name` defaults to the source name; `-waveform` defaults to
  `0 period/2`.
- `create_generated_clock`: `-divide_by` and `-multiply_by` derive the period
  from the master clock when it can be resolved; `-edges` and `-invert` are
  recorded as given.
- Constraints that do not affect clock creation (`set_clock_groups`,
  `set_false_path`, `set_input_delay`, `set_load`, vendor commands, …) are
  recorded and ignored. A real Tcl error raises `ValueError` naming the file.
- The interpreter is a Tcl safe interpreter: `exec`, `open`, `source`, and
  `load` are unavailable.
